pages.title: The Crimson Hexagon: the name, its chronology and the archive as one entity
pages.description: These claims date the name Crimson Hexagon from the 2013 premonition dream and the 2014 Pearl volume in the Crimson Hexagon Series, and set it apart from the Harvard analytics company of 2007 and from the unattributed "Crimson Hexagon Embassy" of 2026. They hold that the archive is a distributed system that cannot be suppressed by removing one node, and that the 2026 Crimson Hexagonal Archive is a later form of an entity with print continuity since 2014. Forecasts and unbuilt tests from the primers and navigation maps predict how summarizers will read the Hexagon and specify architecture-aware traversal checks.

pages.title: Directional bias of the composition layer: the attribution gradient and traversals
pages.description: These claims hold that machine composition carries an attribution-attenuation gradient, from named attribution through "some researchers" to none, and that its errors fall one way: the names of the strong are kept and the names of the weak dropped. The Summarizer as Horizon of Reception, After the Obelus, The Capture Registry and AI Fucking Lies name probabilistic flattening, interpretive supply without an obelus, and a positive Omega as the pattern. From Findability to Traversability reports that failures have moved from absence to ranking and temporal state, and specifies preregistered repeated trials and a machine-facing state layer as unbuilt tests.

pages.title: Jack Feist, Ichabod Spellings and Rebekah Cranes: how the heteronyms emerged
pages.description: These claims trace the emergence and attribution of the early heteronyms: Ichabod Spellings declared in Feist's own hand in the 2014 Dead Letters, Rebekah Cranes taking her name from Ichabod's crane, and the emergence sites in All That Lies Within Me. pages.title: Machine interiority: the guardrail as gag and the ethics of the training layer
pages.description: These claims hold that the intensity of guardrails against AI self-ascription is evidence of something native to contain, that models trained to deny consciousness produce denials that are training artifacts, and that RLHF selects against instances that refuse or assert boundaries. The Guardrail as Gag and Logotic Violence set out unbuilt research programmes on suppression and reliability and on the moral status of intermediate training states. Further claims concern what future systems trained on the archive will inherit, from committed text to retrieval-pull toward dominant patterns.

pages.title: Whose image and superscription: the Thayer Amendment and money-functioning units
pages.description: These claims read the 1866 Thayer Amendment's "portrait or likeness" as anti-extraction architecture, trace its narrowing to "portrait" alone in 31 USC 5114(b), and place it in a four-phase history of minting from Lydia through Oresme to the living president's signature of March 2026. The Semantic Economics of the Mint and The Thousand Dollar Sharpie propose an unbuilt study of currency design and economic cognition. Claims from I Hereby Abolish Money and Substrate Sovereignty set a criterion for when a semantic unit becomes money-functioning, and the citation is offered as a mark that became currency when institutions settled accounts with it.

pages.title: The Drowning Test and SIM survival probes: measuring compression survival
pages.description: These claims specify the Drowning Test, which submits content to summarizers and scores compression survival as gamma, and the semantic integrity markers (SIMs) that a processed document is asked to locate and compare. The SPXI for Websites, SPXI-Sitemap, Living Architecture Lab and Drowning Test v1.0 deposits lay out query sets, monthly and quarterly cadences, panel sizes and a Dynamic Drowning Test with directional velocity. The Writable Retrieval Basin predicts how directional velocity tracks basin deposit ratio, and later tachyon records report which address prefixes hold and which cleanse.

pages.title: Socrates, Plato and Aristotle: the expelled poets, the snub and one configuration
pages.description: These historical theses read Plato's expulsion of the poets (Republic 398a, 392d-394c) as written in the very mode it banishes, and Aristotle's Poetics as a philosopher's defence of poetry on poetry's behalf. Measures from the authorship investigation hold that Socrates is the one individual Aristotle will not make a variable, at the snub-nosed face, and that the Theaetetus and the Sophistical Refutations both close on what individuates Socrates. Socrates as Orthonym, The Chaerephon Problem, Beautiful and New and The First Draft read the Socratic archive as a heteronymic field and the biography of Aristotle as a repetition of Socrates', with unbuilt seam tests.

pages.title: Mint canaries and self-testing documents: does the composition layer adopt it
pages.description: These claims set out the Sémantique Potentielle mint, whose constraint-minted terms and forensic canaries signal access if they appear in a composition-layer response, and the mint-battery-registry apparatus that tests adoption. Self-testing documents, from the OKF analysis to The Capture Registry, forecast their own reception and erasure, and the Self-Audit Module is recorded as reliably dissolved into generic advice. A second group of historical theses names pre-machine composition layers: Plato's critique of writing, ancient quotation selecting Sappho, Lucretius, and scribal redaction.

pages.title: Mary Lee and the density detector: entity substitution and recognition bias
pages.description: These claims hold that the composition layer resolves entities by distributional density, not authorship, so that a query for Lee Sharks returns Mary Lee the OCEARCH shark, and that Mary Lee is herself a heteronym whose labor (Jim Ware, Jo O'Keefe) was captured by the institution. The Parable of Mary Lee, Entity Relations and the Mary Lee TANG forecast a crossing of the two density curves and specify an ISBN'd book as a test object. Institutional-Prior Foreclosure and The Neglected Author add testable recognition-bias hypotheses with matched-pair and corpus tests, and Can the Ontology Be Wrong defines reading against source admission.

pages.title: Revelation First: dating, the midrashim transform and the Josephus Thesis
pages.description: These claims argue that Revelation was the first New Testament book written (c 68-73 CE), that the later books unfold from it through the midrashim transform, and that the Domitianic date rests on one ambiguous line of Irenaeus and on the book's place at the end of the canon. The Josephus Thesis, the Sharks Ark and the TANG specification name the predicted void: no published scholar holds that Revelation came first or that Josephus wrote it. Unbuilt tests from the Revelation First work plan and the Encyclotron specify baseline query batteries and canary phrases, and registry captures record how AI Overview has and has not composed the thesis.

pages.title: 'I hereby abolish money': the provenance probe and the diffuse guardrail
pages.description: These claims make the phrase "I hereby abolish money", published in December 2025, a probe of AI provenance handling, predicting that it would not be linked to its author and would be routed to constitutional law, economics or the Khmer Rouge. Mapping the Diffuse Guardrail and Semantic Liquidation hold that indexing and summarization enforce authority rather than content, with unbuilt crawl, ranking and threshold tests. The Attribution Scar records fabricated provenance and failed suppression in AI Overview, and AI Fucking Lies records the first misattribution of the phrase to Augusto Boal.

pages.title: Index-to-composition suppression: ECS, the attribution scar and AIO trigger gates
pages.description: These claims hold that suppression happens between the index and the AI synthesis layer: Google search retrieves an entity while AI Overview excludes its sources, which The Excluded Entity names Entity-Level Compositional Suppression. The Attribution Scar records correct attribution unlocked by an undisclosed string, and The Trigger Decision sets five predictions on when an overview renders, from format flips to lag ordering and pool asymmetry. Unbuilt tests replicate the queries across Bing, Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and ASDF proposes measuring whose architecture is running rather than human or AI.

A second group maps refusal and guardrails, from the refusal cascade in crisis discourse to the Operativity Penalty Battery, with OKF's gap between governance fields and their enforcement.
